# Process / CLI I/O

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. What CLI tools and containerized services actually need day-to-day (argument parsing, stdin, environment config, exit codes). Prioritized because the long-term project direction favors CLI/microservice use cases. `console.log`/`.error` already write to stdout/stderr respectively — see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md) — the gaps below are everything *else* a CLI program needs.

**Coverage**: 32/32 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 13/32 (~41%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

POSIX recovers the signal from the wait status (`WIFSIGNALED`/`WTERMSIG`); Windows from the signal `child.kill` recorded, since `TerminateProcess` leaves no signalled bit ([ADR-00761](../adr/ADR-00761.md), [TDD-00184](../tdd/TDD-00184.md)) |
| `child_process.fork()` (self-fork + IPC channel) | ✅ | • Self-fork only: the path must be `__filename` or `process.argv[1]` (forking a *different* module would need a second compiled program — clean rejection); the options object must be an empty `{}`<br>• Messages are strings (`send(obj)` is a clean rejection); one `'message'` listener per side<br>• Bare `process.send` reads as a *boolean* forked-ness probe, not Node's function-or-undefined — `assert.strictEqual(process.send, undefined)`-style tests type-mismatch cleanly | • Node's own mechanism ([TDD-00141](../tdd/TDD-00141.md)/[ADR-00425](../adr/ADR-00425.md)): socketpair + re-exec of the current binary with `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` set; child argv layout `[exe, modulePath, ...args]` so extra args land at `argv[2]`; NDJSON string frames (embedded C, linked only when used)<br>• Parent: `child.send(str)→bool`, `child.on('message'/'exit'/'close')`, `child.disconnect()`, inherited stdio; child: `process.send(str)→bool` (false unforked), `process.on('message')` (holds the event loop open while connected), `process.disconnect()`; `mustCall`-wrapped listeners contextually typed<br>• `process.argv[i]` out-of-range reads are a real `undefined` ([ADR-00780](../adr/ADR-00780.md)) — the `argv[2] === 'child'` / `if (!argv[2])` idioms and `=== undefined` all behave as in Node |
| `child_process.spawnSync()` / `.execSync()` / `.execFileSync()` (blocking) | ✅ | • Options object supports `{ cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }` only (no `env`/`timeout`/`input`/`shell`/`stdio` — clean rejections); results are strings (the `encoding: 'utf8'` shape), not Buffers<br>• `spawnSync`'s result carries `status`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`pid` only — no `signal`/`error`/`output` fields (a signal death folds into `status` as `128+signal`)<br>• `execSync`/`execFileSync` throw `Command failed: <command>` on a non-zero exit status ([ADR-00753](../adr/ADR-00753.md)), but the thrown plain `Error` does not yet carry the `.status`/`.stdout`/`.stderr` ExecException properties — use `spawnSync().status` when the exit code or captured output of a failing command is needed | • One embedded C core ([ADR-00411](../adr/ADR-00411.md)): fork + execvp with both stdio pipes poll-multiplexed to completion (no deadlock when a child fills stderr while stdout drains), then a blocking waitpid; `execSync` runs via `/bin/sh -c`<br>• `execSync`/`execFileSync` throw on a non-zero exit and return the captured stdout only on success, matching Node ([ADR-00753](../adr/ADR-00753.md))<br>• Distinct from the bespoke `process.execFileSync` above (which throws on failure and inherits stderr) |
